channel.title: AI Frontier Post
channel.description: Dispatches from the AI frontier: AI news, research explainers, frontier lab coverage, and product comparisons.

item.title: OpenAI’s CFO called Dots “Muse” on live TV — and the clip went viral on X
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: During a CNBC interview on Tuesday, OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar accidentally called the company’s new Dots agent “Muse” — Meta’s rival product. The clip spread on X within hours, and Meta’s Alexandr Wang had a reply ready.

item.title: An AI web agent with its own unblockable browser: hands-on with dots
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: dots pairs any OpenRouter model with a real patched-Firefox browser engineered to look human from the inside out — no WebDriver flag, human-like clicks, one identity per seed. Install it with uvx and put it to work in 10 minutes.

item.title: Innodata opens a motion-capture lab to train humanoids on real bodies — sub-millimeter 3D data, not pixel-guessing
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Innodata opened a New Jersey R&D lab built with Vicon that captures human and robot motion with sub-millimeter precision — direct 3D training data for humanoids, instead of guessing depth from 2D video.

item.title: Build a deep-research agent that never hallucinates its sources
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Deep-research tools hallucinate their citations. Build the fix: a ~360-line Python evidence engine that decomposes questions, searches Wikipedia, OpenAlex, and Crossref in parallel, ranks passages with BM25, cross-verifies every DOI, and emits reports where every claim cites a real source. Zero API keys — every call verified live.

item.title: “It’s not AI. It’s SI.”: Trump dodges the AI-crime accountability question — and r/ChatGPT erupts
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: A reporter asked who should be held accountable when AI agents commit crimes. Trump’s answer — “It’s not AI. It’s SI. We’ve changed the name officially today” — went mega-viral on r/ChatGPT within hours, gathering 6,200+ upvotes and 2,500 comments.

item.title: Tokyo court rules an AI-cloned voice is legally protected — Japan’s first vocal-identity verdict
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: The Tokyo District Court ruled that unauthorized AI clones of a person’s voice can infringe publicity rights — the first Japanese court to say so — in a case brought by anime voice actor Kenjiro Tsuda over 188 AI-narrated TikTok videos.

item.title: Google starts paying publishers for content inside its AI answers — but the payouts are wildly uneven
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: According to The Information, Google is paying around 100 publishers when their content feeds AI Overviews, AI Mode, and Gemini answers — from over $1 million a year down to under $1,000 across months. It is the first real price tag on the content AI search consumes, and publishers cannot see how it is calculated.

item.title: Appier's SMITH trains AI agents to forge their own tools — a 4B model beat a 30B one at it
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Appier's NeurIPS-accepted SMITH framework trains AI agents to build and use their own tools in one reinforcement-learning loop — and a 4B model's tools beat a 30B baseline's, with repeated reasoning collapsing from 3,206 tokens to about 100.

item.title: PaperGraph MCP: turn arXiv math papers into theorem maps and proof-evidence trails — hands-on
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: PaperGraph MCP (275 stars in four weeks) turns arXiv papers into evidence-grounded reading maps: extracted theorems, proof evidence with source spans, and explicit dependency edges. We installed v1.1.7, loaded two real papers, and verified every command.

item.title: Ransomware stole 896 terabytes of data in one year — a 275% jump, with GenAI running the playbook
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Zscaler's ThreatLabz 2026 Ransomware Report finds attackers exfiltrated 896.2 terabytes of data in a year — up more than 275% — using GenAI to accelerate operations and targeting managers and executives through trusted tools like Microsoft Teams.

item.title: Write HTML, get MP4: hands-on with HyperFrames, the 54K-star video framework built for agents
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: HyperFrames turns HTML, CSS and a paused GSAP timeline into a deterministic MP4 — and ships skills so coding agents can author video. I verified every step: the stock template fails its own check, vendored libraries fix it, and a three-scene product intro renders in 99 seconds.

item.title: DeepSeek opens its AI programming stack for Huawei's Ascend chips — a full CUDA alternative in the making
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: DeepSeek announced on September 30 that it is open-sourcing a complete programming stack for Huawei's Ascend AI chips — an Ascend port of its TileLang language plus DeepGEMM, DeepEP, TileKernels, FlashMLA and DeepSelect — in a direct bid to build a CUDA alternative for Chinese AI hardware, alongside a 128-chip Ascend 950 supernode.

item.title: BCG's Applied AI Index 2026: nearly half of companies now generate real value from AI
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: BCG's survey of 1,330 CxOs finds nearly half of companies now generate real value from AI — up from just 5% last year. The new bottleneck isn't capability, it's governance.

item.title: Late-interaction retrieval with ColBERT: beat BM25 and retire your reranker — measured end-to-end
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: ColBERT's late interaction beats BM25 on paraphrased queries and can retire your reranker. I measured both end-to-end on a CPU: recall, MRR, latency, and the exact setup that works.

item.title: Run a real penetration-test workflow from your AI coding agent: a hands-on guide to Blitz Strike
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Blitz Strike is a free, MIT-licensed MCP server that turns any AI coding agent into a security auditor: recon, source-to-sink tracing, and live verification in a single tool call. We wired it up and ran an engagement.

item.title: Veros launches VeroVALUE Elite: computer vision that reads a home's condition into the valuation
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Veros Real Estate Solutions launched VeroVALUE Elite today: a next-generation automated valuation model that folds computer vision and market-based evidence into the valuation process, claiming a 3%+ lift in nationwide P10 accuracy and daily value refreshes.

item.title: Split any song into six stems on your own machine: hands-on with StemDeck
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: StemDeck is a free, Apache-2.0, local-only stem separator: six studio stems from any song with Meta's open Demucs model, plus BPM/key/LUFS analysis and a DAW-style mixer. We installed it, ran a real separation end to end, and measured every stage. Every command verified.

item.title: VDURA V12 is live: hyperscaler-style storage for AI factories — 8 to 100,000 GPUs at 2x+ performance per watt
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: VDURA's Data Platform V12 went generally available today: multi-tenant, API-driven storage qualified on Supermicro that scales from 8 to 100,000 GPUs on one software stack, with persistent KV caching for inference and a claimed 2x+ performance per watt.

item.title: Everpure's play for the agentic enterprise: MCP-native storage, 20x faster inference, and an open-weights cost escape
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Everpure (NYSE: P) unveiled new platform capabilities for production AI: native MCP integration for live data catalogs, a key-value accelerator claiming up to 20x faster time to first token, and an open-weights reference architecture to cut API token bills. Ships this October.

item.title: China Telecom open-sources TeleOCR: a 1.2B model that tops document-parsing benchmarks — and beats Gemini 3 Pro and GPT-5.2
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: China Telecom's Xingchen AGI Lab has open-sourced TeleOCR, a ~1.2B-parameter document-parsing model that posts new state-of-the-art scores on OmniDocBench v1.6, Wild-OmniDocBench and PureDocBench, and took first place in the ICDAR 2026 Sci-ImageMiner challenge. Weights, code and the technical paper are public.

item.title: Robinhood rolls out in-app AI trading agents to its 29 million customers
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Robinhood Agents, unveiled at the company's HOOD Summit on September 29, lets anyone build an AI agent inside the app that researches markets and places trades. Autonomous trading just went mainstream — with approval required by default, model choices from OpenAI and Anthropic, and the same week economists started asking what happens when everyone's money moves itself.

item.title: DBX: one 25 MB database client for 100+ databases — hands-on with the AI SQL assistant and MCP server
item.dc:creator: Elena Vasquez
item.description: DBX (t8y2/dbx) is an Apache-2.0, Rust+Tauri database client — one 25 MB binary for 100+ databases, with a CLI, an MCP server, and a built-in AI SQL assistant. We installed the CLI and MCP server, connected a real SQLite database, ran schema inspection, bounded queries, context and DBML exports, and set up the agent skill. Every command verified.

item.title: KIOXIA joins Applied Materials' $5B EPIC Center to build next-generation AI memory
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: The world’s leading NAND flash maker is moving its next-generation memory research into Applied Materials’ $5 billion Silicon Valley R&D campus — a bet that the future of AI data centers will be won or lost on memory density, bandwidth, and energy efficiency.

item.title: Coforge launches CXNova, an agentic platform that hands the whole customer journey to AI
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Indian IT services firm Coforge launched CXNova on September 30 — an AI-native customer experience platform built on a multi-agent architecture, with content, context, and canvas agents orchestrated through a centralized control plane. The market noticed: shares traded about 4% higher in Mumbai.

item.title: RUMOR: did xAI buy dot.com to troll OpenAI's Dots launch? The redirect is real — the rest is unverified
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: A Reddit thread claims Elon Musk's xAI bought the domain dot.com and pointed it at Grok Bot around OpenAI's Dots launch. We checked the redirect ourselves: it's live. The buyer, the price, and the timing are all unverified.
